name: Virginia security engineer seeking sustainable hours

context.geography: Virginia, US; local hybrid or eligible US remote
constraints: Civilian product companies and selected defense contractors
context.company_awareness: Some product employers known; assumes many nearby contractors require clearance but will inspect exceptions.

trigger: Another overnight operational escalation makes the engineer search for application or product security work, but nearby results repeatedly mention active clearances.

searches_run.query: cybersecurity engineer jobs Virginia no clearance required
searches_run.observation: Retrieval included a no-clearance Indeed landing page containing clearance-required titles, a purported Amentum no-clearance opening, and SAIC employer search. Amentum returned 404 when opened. Direct SAIC inspection showed an explicit None clearance facet alongside other categories.

searches_run.query: security engineer jobs no on call no SOC shifts
searches_run.observation: Results included Indeed and discussion threads about on-call and shifts. The no-on-call Indeed result still mentioned a SOC analyst. These results do not establish which employers offer daytime-only work.

sources.title: Virginia Careers | SAIC
sources.supports: Direct inspection found clearance None, remote-work filters and employer job-alert form; shows contractors cannot be excluded wholesale.

best_entry_page.primary_query: cybersecurity engineer jobs Virginia no clearance required
best_entry_page.promise: Find covered employers and learn to distinguish explicitly stated clearance and shift requirements from missing details.
best_entry_page.cta: Choose covered security employers and create role alerts; inspect original requirements before applying.
proof_needed: Examples of explicit no-clearance versus active-clearance language
Coverage of civilian product employers and relevant contractor roles
Separate handling of shift work and on-call
A visible unknown state where source text is silent

conversion_objections: Will no-clearance search still include active Secret requirements?
No SOC shifts does not automatically mean no on-call.
Will a description check silently assume missing text means no requirement?
Why pay for a filter if employer career sites already have clearance categories?

avoid_targeting.reason: Work schedules cannot be guaranteed from absent posting details.

message_to_founder: Simulation: I would pay attention to fewer plausible openings, not a larger security-job count. Show the actual clearance and hours wording, let me keep unknowns separate, and do not discard every contractor just because of its industry.
